name: absorbent
entries: {@i The armor is padded with thick batting made from special absorbent fibers. This tends to wipe clean any sharp objects that penetrate it.}
The wearer of this armor has resistance to poison damage from poison-coated weapons, but not from the fangs of creatures that inject their venom as they bite.

entries.name: Academic Tradition
entries: The runes of mages, scholars, and elves, these traditions are not necessarily any less ancient, but runecarvers of these traditions seek new knowledge and expression, rather than being rooted in the old ways. Your ability modifier for this tradition is Intelligence, and you can select your related tool from {@item Calligrapher's Supplies|PHB} or {@item Woodcarver's Tools|PHB}.

entries.name: Accurate
entries: This weapon, when used to make ranged attacks, reduces by 1 point the Armor Class benefit an opponent derives from half {@quickref cover|PHB|3} or three-quarter cover.

entries.name: Adaptable
entries: This weapon can be used with differing techniques, allowing it to deal different types of damage. A damage type in parentheses appears with the property— when a creature makes a weapon attack with this weapon, it can choose to deal the weapon's alternative damage type.

entries.name: Aerodynamic
entries: A weapon with the ammunition property adds +10/40 to its range increments. A weapon with the ballistic property adds +10/30 while a weapon with the thrown property adds +5/15.

entries.name: Alternate (B)
entries: When you wish, you can employ bludgeoning damage with no change to the weapon's damage dice. Doing so does not reduce the weapon's efficiency or convert it into an improvised weapon.

entries.name: Alternate (B)
entries: {@i Alternate weapons have multiple effective striking surfaces.}
When you attack, you can employ the listed alternate damage type with no change to the weapon's damage dice. Doing so does not reduce the weapon's efficiency or convert it into an improvised weapon.

entries.name: Alternate (P)
entries: When you wish, you can employ piercing damage with no change to the weapon's damage dice. Doing so does not reduce the weapon's efficiency or convert it into an improvised weapon.

entries.name: Alternate (P)
entries: {@i Alternate weapons have multiple effective striking surfaces.}
When you attack, you can employ the listed alternate damage type with no change to the weapon's damage dice. Doing so does not reduce the weapon's efficiency or convert it into an improvised weapon.

entries.name: Alternate (P)
entries: When you wish, you can employ slashing damage with no change to the weapon's damage dice. Doing so does not reduce the weapon's efficiency or convert it into an improvised weapon.

entries.name: Alternate (S)
entries: {@i Alternate weapons have multiple effective striking surfaces.}
When you attack, you can employ the listed alternate damage type with no change to the weapon's damage dice. Doing so does not reduce the weapon's efficiency or convert it into an improvised weapon.

entries.name: Ammunition
entries: The ammunition of a firearm is destroyed upon use.

entries.name: Ancient Tradition
entries: The runes of the Giants, Dwarves, and other ancient traditions. Your ability modifier for this tradition is Wisdom, and you can select your related tool from {@item Mason's Tools|PHB} or {@item Painter's Supplies|PHB}.

name: Area of Effect
entries: This weapon's ammunition explodes when it hits a target and may hit nearby creatures standing as well. Each other creature within a number of feet equal to the AOE range (noted in parentheses) must make a Dexterity saving throw with a DC of 13 or 10 + the attacker's proficiency bonus, whichever is higher. On a failed save, the creature takes half of the damage taken by the target.

entries.name: Armor-Piercing
entries: An Armor-Piercing weapon is a Melee weapon designed to punch through armor or thick hide. When you make an attack roll using an Armor-Piercing weapon, you gain a +1 bonus to the attack roll if your target is wearing armor or has an {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} of 18 or higher.

entries.name: Artillery
entries: You must use Strength instead of Dexterity for the attack rolls and damage rolls of a weapon with the Artillery property, and you can use the weapon to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Weapons with the Artillery property must be reloaded with an action. After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

entries.name: Artillery
entries: You must use Strength instead of Dexterity for the Firearm save DC and the attack and damage rolls of this weapon. Such a weapon can be fired once before it must be reloaded with an action.

entries.name: Artillery
entries: You must use Strength instead of Dexterity for the attack rolls and damage rolls of a weapon with the Artillery property, and you can use the weapon to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Weapons with the Artillery property must be reloaded with an action. After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

entries.name: Attached
entries: You can't be disarmed of this weapon, but donning or doffing the weapon takes an action. You can use a hand equipped with this weapon to hold items, but can't attack with the weapon while doing so. Additionally, you have {@bold disadvantage} on attack rolls using other weapons held in a hand equipped with this weapon and on {@skill Sleight of Hand} checks using the hand that is equipped with this weapon.

entries.name: Autofire
entries: A weapon that has the autofire property can only spray in a 10-foot-cube area within range by using 10 pieces of ammunition. Each creature in the area you can see must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking the weapon's normal damage on a failed save. {@b The DC equals to 8 + your proficiency bonus (if proficient with the weapon) + your Dexterity modifier}. Any targets within long range have advantage on this roll.

entries.name: Ballistic
entries: You can use a firearm that has the ballistic property to make a ranged attack only if it is loaded with ammunition. Each time you attack with the firearm, you expend one piece of ammunition. This means a combination of a load (a ball or a weight of shot pellets) and a charge (a measured weight of gunpowder). Alternately, a cartridge of any kind constitutes a piece of ammunition.

A firearm without the magazine weapon property can load only a single piece of ammunition in each of its barrels. If you run out of ammunition, you cannot make additional attacks with the weapon, even if you have a feature that allows you to make additional attacks with that action, bonus action, or reaction. You must reload the firearm before you can use it again.

Weapons with this property require two hands to reload. Reloading a piece of ammunition (powder from a horn and a bullet), requires an action. Barrel-loaded firearms with multiple barrels require each to be reloaded separately. The addition of the magazine property can quicken this process, as described below.

Weapons with this property have two ranges shown in parentheses. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second indicates the weapon's maximum range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the weapon's long range.
If you use a weapon that has the ballistic property to make a melee attack, you treat the weapon as an {@book improvised weapon|CompEquipMan|3|improvised weapons}.

entries.name: Bandolier
entries: When making a ranged attack with a weapon that has the bandolier property, you can immediately draw another weapon of the same type as part of the attack.

entries.name: Barrel
entries: A Barrel weapon can be fired a number of times equal to the number of bullets its barrel can hold (written as Barrel X) before it must be reloaded. It can be reloaded as either an action or instead of an attack as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action. If the weapon also has the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property, it can also be reloaded as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You must have one free hand to reload the weapon.

entries.name: Barrel
entries: The weapon can be fired a number of times equal to the number of bullets its barrel can hold (written as Barrel X) before it must be reloaded according to its fast or slow reload property (F or S, respectively).

entries.name: Barrel
entries: A Barrel weapon can be fired a number of times equal to the number of bullets its barrel can hold (written as Barrel X) before it must be reloaded. It can be reloaded as either an action or instead of an attack as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action. If the weapon also has the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property, it can also be reloaded as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You must have one free hand to reload the weapon.

entries.name: Blackpowder
entries: Blackpowder weapons fire projectiles with ear-splitting noise, shredding armor with deadly force. When fired, Blackpowder weapons emit a deafening crack audible 300 feet away. A Blackpowder weapon exposed to heavy rain, submerged, or similarly drenched in water, can't fire until dried for 1 hour. These weapons use paper cartridge bullets as ammunition.

entries.name: Blackpowder
entries: Whenever you make an attack roll with this weapon, the weapon emits a thundering boom audible up to the weapon's long range. Additionally, when you make an attack roll with this weapon and roll a 1 on the {@dice d20}, you are {@condition deafened} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Blaring
entries: Firing a Blaring weapon makes a thunderous crack. The sound can be heard from up to 100 feet away. Making a ranged attack using a weapon with this property makes it hard to go undetected; you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks made as part of the {@action Hide|XPHB} action until the start of your next turn. In addition, if a creature is within the area of the sound blast, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made against you as part of the {@action Search|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Blaring
entries: Firing this weapon makes a thunderous crack. The sound can be heard from up to 100 feet away. Firing a weapon with this property makes it hard to go undetected; you have disadvantage on {@skill Stealth} checks to hide until the start of your next turn. In addition, if a creature is within the area of the sound blast, it has advantage on {@skill Perception} checks against you.

entries.name: Blaring
entries: Firing a Blaring weapon makes a thunderous crack. The sound can be heard from up to 100 feet away. Making a ranged attack using a weapon with this property makes it hard to go undetected; you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks made as part of the {@action Hide|XPHB} action until the start of your next turn. In addition, if a creature is within the area of the sound blast, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made against you as part of the {@action Search|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Blast
entries: This property is applied to a weapon by its ammunition, only for the attacks that make use of such ammunition. These attacks are made with advantage, increasing the weapon's reliability against close targets and offsetting the disadvantage applied to long-range targets.

Attacking a target within the weapon's long range increment (beyond its normal range), lets you designate a secondary target within 5 feet of the primary target and apply your attack and damage roll to both. Choose both targets before rolling to hit.
Attacks with this ammunition do not apply your ability modifier to damage unless the modifier is negative. Nor are these attacks subtle or precise enough to apply a rogue's Sneak Attack damage.

entries.name: Blaster
entries: A weapon with the Blaster property is a Ranged weapon that requires no ammunition. This property counts as {@itemProperty A|XPHB|Ammunition}.

entries.name: Blaster
entries: A weapon with the Blaster property is a Ranged weapon that requires no ammunition. This property counts as {@itemProperty A|XPHB|Ammunition}.

entries.name: Blaster
entries: A weapon with the Blaster property is a Ranged weapon that requires no ammunition. This property counts as {@itemProperty A|XPHB|Ammunition}.

entries.name: Booming
entries: The deflagration from firing a Booming weapon makes a stupendous booming sound. The sound can be heard from up to 500 feet away. Making a ranged attack using a weapon with this property makes it impossible to go undetected; you automatically fail Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks made as part of the {@action Hide|XPHB} action until the start of your next turn. In addition, if a creature is within the area of the sound blast, it automatically succeeds on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made against you as part of the {@action Search|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Booming
entries: The deflagration from firing this weapon makes a stupendous booming sound. The sound can be heard from up to 500 feet away. Firing this weapon makes it impossible to go undetected; you automatically fail {@skill Stealth} checks to hide until the start of your next turn. In addition, if a creature is within the area of the sound blast, it automatically succeeds on {@skill Perception} checks against you.

entries.name: Booming
entries: The deflagration from firing a Booming weapon makes a stupendous booming sound. The sound can be heard from up to 500 feet away. Making a ranged attack using a weapon with this property makes it impossible to go undetected; you automatically fail Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks made as part of the {@action Hide|XPHB} action until the start of your next turn. In addition, if a creature is within the area of the sound blast, it automatically succeeds on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made against you as part of the {@action Search|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Braced
entries: When making an attack with a Braced weapon, use your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls. If the weapon has the {@itemProperty H|XPHB|Heavy} property, use your Strength score to determine if you can use it without {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Breach
entries: If this property is applied to a weapon by its ammunition, it applies only for the attacks that make use of such ammunition. Breach allows attacks to ignore up to 1 point of a target's protection from armor. The attack recalculates accordingly the target's armor benefit (AC points derived from armor, natural armor, and shields). This does not affect AC bonuses derived from other sources like Dexterity modifiers, class features, or magical enhancements.
If this property is noted with a number (as in the case of some firearms), the breach effect ignores up to the stated number of points of the target's protection from armor.

entries.name: Burst
entries: As an action, you can expend 10 shots of a Burst weapon's ammunition to spray shots in a 10-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} within the weapon's normal range. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take damage. Roll the weapon's damage once, and apply it to each creature that failed the save.

entries.name: Burst Fire
entries: A weapon that has the burst fire property can make a normal single-target attack, or it can spray a 10-foot-cube area within normal range by using 10 pieces of ammunition. Each creature in the area you can see must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking the weapon's normal damage on a failed save. {@b The DC equals to 8 + your proficiency bonus (if proficient with the weapon) + your Dexterity modifier}.

entries.name: Close Quarters
entries: Being within 5 feet of an enemy doesn't impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on your ranged attack rolls with a Close Quarters weapon.

entries.name: Close Quarters Battle (CQB)
entries: If you hit a creature within 15 feet or less from you, you can add an extra die to the damage roll.

entries.name: Concealed
entries: You have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) checks to conceal this weapon.

entries.name: Concussive
entries: These weapons bludgeon as much as they pierce. When determining a creature's resistance or immunity to damage from this weapon, use the weaker of the target's resistance or immunity to piercing or to bludgeoning damage. For instance, if a creature is immune to piercing damage and has no resistance or immunity to bludgeoning damage, it would take full damage from a concussive weapon. Resistance to all physical damage applies as normal.

entries.name: Cooldown
entries: Because this weapon requires cooldown time between uses, you can only fire it once when you use an action, {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you normally make. This property counts as {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading}.

entries.name: Cooldown
entries: Because this weapon requires cooldown time between uses, you can only fire it once when you use an action, {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you normally make. This property counts as {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading}.

entries.name: Cooldown
entries: Because this weapon requires cooldown time between uses, you can only fire it once when you use an action, {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you normally make. This property counts as {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading}.

entries.name: Covert
entries: You have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) checks to conceal this weapon.

entries.name: Cruel
entries: If this property is applied to a weapon by its ammunition, it applies only for the attacks that make use of such ammunition. Each successful attack with a cruel weapon leaves a piece (or the entirety) of the weapon or ammunition in the wound. Removing the object requires an action and a successful {@dc 8} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check, with each failure inflicting 1 additional point of damage.
For each piece of cruel ammunition currently in a target, temporarily reduce its maximum hit points by 1 and increase the DC of any Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) checks to stabilize it by 1.
Cruel ammunition is always destroyed when used; you cannot recover any intact pieces after a battle as you might with normal ammunition.

entries.name: Cumbersome
entries: A shield with the cumbersome property can't be effectively thrown regardless of its wielder's class features or other abilities.

entries.name: Cumbersome
entries: Cumbersome weapons are difficult to wield but are effective ranged tools for those strong enough to wield them. When making an attack with a Cumbersome weapon, you must use your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls.

entries.name: Lingering Curses
entries: Ending your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a Cursed Curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. If you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}.

entries.name: Damage
entries: A Damage property weapon can deal different types of damage. When you hit with an attack from this weapon, choose one of the damage types allowed.

entries.name: Deadly
entries: With any successful attack, you can reroll up to one of the weapon's damage dice if it rolls a 1. You cannot reroll any die that has already been rerolled with another effect (such as the {@optfeature Great Weapon Fighting|PHB} class feature or the {@feat Savage Attacker} feat) and vice versa.

entries.name: Deep Lead
entries: Lead as a metal is known to be a natural counter to magic. The thinnest sheet of lead can block the most powerful of divination, and it is often used as a mean to protect against magical prying. A purer form of lead, called deep lead or sometimes dimeritium, exists. It is a silvery metal with a hint of blue found only rarely in mineral veins. Deep lead is highly toxic, and those frequently exposed to it regularly experience migraines, respiratory diseases or even seizures. These effects are amplified for magical creatures and spellcasters that will instantly feel nauseous in its presence and intense physical pain at its contact. Witch Hunters rely heavily on deep lead and have integrated in their arsenal several devices based on that metal to face their most dangerous enemy: spellcasters.

entries.name: Defensive
entries: If you are wielding a weapon with this property and another creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add a +1 bonus to your Armor Class for that attack only, potentially causing the attack to miss you. If you are wielding two weapons with this property, the bonus is instead +2. This bonus to Armor Class is not compatible with the bonus from a {@item Shield (*)|CompEquipMan|shield} nor does it combine with the benefits of the {@feat Defensive Duelist} feat.

entries.name: Defensive
entries: While you wield one or more weapons with this property, you gain a +1 bonus to AC if you are proficient in the weapon and not using a shield.

entries.name: Destructible
entries: After you make an attack with this weapon, it is destroyed.

entries.name: Destructible
entries: After you make an attack with this weapon, it is destroyed.

entries.name: Detonator
entries: Every planted explosive needs a detonator, and it can be detonated manually, automatically or after a determined time depending on the detonator used.

entries.name: Disarming
entries: When wielding this weapon, you gain a +2 bonus on attack rolls to {@action disarm|DMG}. Increase this bonus to +3 if the weapon is two-handed or is versatile and used in two hands, or if you are wielding two single-handed weapons that each have this property. (These benefits do not apply to a {@optfeature Disarming Attack|PHB} Combat Maneuver, which uses unrelated techniques to both disarm and inflict damage with the same strike.)

entries.name: Double
entries: A Double weapon functions as two {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} weapons, one in each hand, for the purposes of two-weapon fighting. If a Double weapon has {@itemProperty R|XPHB|Reach}, you can use only one of these properties per turn.

entries.name: Double
entries: A double weapon has two striking ends on either side of an elongated grip. It is too unwieldy for Small creatures to handle properly; they have disadvantage on attack rolls with double-ended weapons. When you use your {@action Attack} action to make an attack with a double-ended weapon, you can also use a bonus action to make an additional attack with it. You don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus action attack, unless that modifier is negative.
If you have the {@optfeature Two-Weapon Fighting} fighting style or {@feat Dual Wielder} feat, you gain all of their benefits while wielding a double weapon, as if it were two different weapons.

name: efficient
entries: {@i This suit of armor is cunningly designed to be much easier to put on or remove.}
Halve the normal time necessary to {@table Donning and Doffing Armor|CompEquipMan|don or doff} such armor.

name: enclosed
entries: {@i This armor's design mostly encloses the body with protective materials that are more impervious to liquid.}

The wearer has resistance to damage from any liquids contacted (unless completely submerged), including contact poisons, defoliant, holy water, and the like. Caustic substances like acid and alchemist's fire are not affected because their damage does not rely on absorption through the skin or a mystical reaction caused by contact with the flesh.

name: ersatz
entries: If the wearer of this armor suffers a critical hit, and it was not delivered by a weapon with the ersatz weapon property, the armor sustains significant damage. This penalty applies even if the critical hit is downgraded to a normal hit because of some magic, class feature, or other special equipment.

For every such hit, the armor suffers a permanent and cumulative –1 penalty to the AC it offers. Armor reduced to a protective rating of 10 is destroyed such that it no longer provides an Armor Class rating when worn.
A crafter using the applicable artisan's tools can repair damaged or destroyed ersatz armor. Each –1 penalty applied is repaired at a cost of 5% of the armor's value.

entries.name: Ersatz
entries: If the d20 for your attack roll with this weapon produces a 1, the weapon suffers significant damage; in addition to the attack automatically missing, the weapon suffers a permanent and cumulative –1 penalty to damage rolls. If the penalty gets to –5, the weapon is destroyed.
A crafter using the applicable artisan's tools can repair this weapon if it has not yet been destroyed. Each –1 penalty applied is repaired at a cost of 5% of the weapon's normal value.
Attacks made using ammunition with the ersatz property have a –1 penalty to damage. Whether it hits or misses, such ammunition is destroyed when used; none of it can be collected after the battle.

name: Example Template
entries: {@note This is an example {@book Blacksmithing|KTKCG|12} template weapon.}

name: Exotic
entries: {@note See {@book Appendix E: Exotic Materials|KTKCG|26}.}

entries.name: Fabled Heirloom
entries: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the {@table Heirloom Rarity|CrookedMoon24} table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

entries.name: Fan Fire
entries: You can quickly fire this weapon by slamming the hammer repeatedly. As an action, you fire a number of bullets in a row equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum of 2, up to the entirety of the barrel). Each attack after the first suffers a cumulative −3 penalty to the attack roll. You cannot add any modifier to the damage roll of these attacks beyond the first (such as the bonus from your Dexterity modifier, the {@feat Sharpshooter|SGttEH} feat, or a magic weapon's bonus to damage rolls). When you use this action, your speed becomes 0 until the end of your turn, and attacks you make using the long range of the weapon automatically miss.

If you roll a 1 on any of the attack rolls, the weapon jams and can't be used again until it is repaired. You can use an action to make a {@dc 15} {@skill Sleight of Hand} check, repairing the weapon on a success. Alternatively, you can spend 1 hour outside of combat to mend it, automatically succeeding on the check. If your check fails, the weapon is broken and must be mended in a specialist's store at a quarter of the cost of the firearm.

entries.name: Fan Fire
entries: You can quickly fire this weapon by slamming the hammer repeatedly. As an action, you fire a number of bullets in a row equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum of 2, up to the entirety of the barrel). Each attack after the first suffers a cumulative -3 penalty to the attack roll. You cannot add any modifier to the damage roll of these attacks beyond the first (such as the bonus from your Dexterity modifier or a magic weapon's bonus to damage rolls). When you take this action, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 0 until the end of your turn, and attacks you make using the long range of the weapon automatically miss.

If you roll a 1 on any of the attack rolls, the weapon jams and can't be used again until it is repaired. You can take an action to make a DC 15 Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check, repairing the weapon on a success. Alternatively, you can spend 1 hour mending it to automatically succeed on the check. If your check fails, the weapon is broken and must be mended in a specialist's store at a quarter of the cost of the firearm.

entries.name: Fast Reload
entries: You must use an attack, an action, or a bonus action to reload this firearm. You must have one free hand to do so.

name: Fell Weapon
entries: A fell weapon can act as an arcane focus.

name: Field Dependency
entries: A weapon or upgrade with this property won't function if the myrmidon's power field has collapsed or if the myrmidon doesn't have a power field.

entries.name: Fine
entries: Double the weapon's object hardness (if any) and its hit points.

entries.name: Firearm
entries: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

entries.name: Firearm
entries: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

entries.name: Gargantuan
entries: These weapons are designed for Gargantuan creatures. They are normally unusable by Huge or smaller creatures.

entries.name: Hafted
entries: A Hafted weapon's haft can function well as an off-hand attack. After you use the {@action Attack|XPHB} action to attack with a Hafted weapon, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make a melee attack with the haft. The haft deals {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage, and you add your ability modifier to damage.

entries.name: Handgun
entries: Handguns are single-handed weapons easily wielded in close combat. Any firearm with this weapon property does not suffer disadvantage for its use when a hostile creature is within 5 feet.

Light weapons with the handgun property allow you to employ the rules for two-weapon fighting. When you take the Attack action and attack with a light weapon that you're holding in one hand, you can use a bonus action to attack with a light weapon that you're holding in your other hand if it has the handgun weapon property. You don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless it is negative

name: hardened
entries: The plating of this armor is particularly resistant to forceful penetration; the wearer's Armor Class is not penalized for attacks made with the {@item breach weapon|CompEquipMan|breach} weapon property. To be fully protected, a shieldbearing creature must have this property on both its armor and shield, since the breach property can act against the protection provided by either one.

entries.name: Heavy
entries: Creatures with a strength score below 13 have disadvantage on attack rolls with Heavy Weapons.

entries.name: High Caliber
entries: You can only make one attack with this weapon when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, and only as the first attack you make on your turn. Once you make an attack with this weapon, you can't make any attacks until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: High-Critical
entries: If the d20 roll for an attack with this weapon is a 20, your critical hit inflicts significant damage. Any damage dice rolled for the attack that come up as 1s are instead treated as 2s. This benefit does not apply to critical hits scored on d20 rolls other than 20, such as might occur with the {@subclassFeature Improved Critical|Fighter|PHB|Champion|PHB|3|PHB} class feature or similar effects.

entries.name: Hooked
entries: When you use the attack action to make an attack with this weapon and you hit your target, instead of dealing damage, you can immediately use a bonus action to attempt to shove that creature. You have advantage on this shove attempt.

entries.name: Huge
entries: These weapons are designed for Huge creatures. They are normally unusable by Large or smaller creatures.

name: Iosan
entries: This weapon is of Iosan manufacture. Iosan guns use a single-powder system devised by elven alchemists, giving them a longer range at the cost of lower impact. Iosan ammunition is incompatible with non-Iosan weapons. A character not proficient with simple or martial weapons of this type has disadvantage the first time they use this weapon.

entries.name: Large
entries: These weapons are designed for Large creatures. They are normally unusable by Medium or smaller creatures.

name: layered
entries: {@i Rather than relying upon a single layer of protective material, this armor uses multiple protective layers cleverly constructed to divert and trap missiles (or their fragments) that would otherwise stick in the wearer's body.}

Attacks with {@item cruel weapon|CompEquipMan|cruel weapons} do not stick in the armor wearer or leave behind pieces that must be removed. A {@item harpoon|CompEquipMan} requires at least 10 points of damage for it to bind and restrain the armor wearer.

name: lightweight
entries: {@i This armor is constructed with expensive, lighter materials.}
Light or medium armor reduces its weight by 4 pounds and removes the disadvantage to Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks, if any.
Heavy armor reduces its weight by 10 pounds and removes the Strength requirement.
A lightweight shield halves its weight and removes the Strength requirement, if any.

entries.name: Limited
entries: Possession of this weapon is restricted in some societies, often requiring a special dispensation, rank, or permit.

entries.name: Loud
entries: Your weapon rings with thunder that is audible within 300 feet of you whenever it makes an attack.

entries.name: Loud
entries: The sound of the weapon (typically a firearm) discharging alerts all hearing creatures within a number of feet as specified by the number in parentheses after the loud property. This range is doubled in echoey locations, such as cave systems, and where sound travels faster, such as underwater.

entries.name: Loud
entries: The sound of the weapon (typically a firearm) being used to make a ranged attack is audible to creatures within a number of feet as specified by the number in parentheses after the Loud property. This range is doubled in echoey locations, such as cave systems, and where sound travels faster, such as underwater.

entries.name: Magazine
entries: A firearm with this property can hold up to the number of rounds listed parenthetically after this weapon property. Without this property, a firearm can load only one round at a time per barrel.

As an action, you can load a number of cartridges, shotshells, or slugs equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum of 1) into the magazine of a firearm you are holding. As a bonus action, you can load a single cartridge, shotshell, or slug into the magazine of a firearm you are holding, regardless of Dexterity or other factors.

entries.name: Magazine
entries: A weapon with the Magazine property also has a number and an ammunition type. The weapon holds that amount and type of ammunition, which you can expend before needing to reload the weapon. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you may remove a {@item Magazine|GrimHollowPG24} and then reload it with a new {@item Magazine|GrimHollowPG24}. A {@item Magazine|GrimHollowPG24} weapon comes with two empty magazines included in the weapon's cost and weight. An additional empty magazine for a Magazine weapon costs 25 GP. Loading an empty Magazine with ammunition takes 1 minute.

name: Magelock
entries: A magelock weapon is specially hardened against the effects of a gun mage's rune shots. While in the hands of a gun mage, a magelock weapon is a magic weapon.

entries.name: Misfire
entries: If the d20 for your attack roll produces a 1, the barrel of a weapon with this property is fouled; in addition to the attack automatically missing, the barrel is rendered inoperable and the ammunition is destroyed. A fouled barrel must be cleaned and recharged before it can be used again. This cleaning takes 15 minutes and requires tinker's tools.
Each loaded barrel of a firearm from the Firearms 1 or 2 limited lists (weapons not using sealed metal cartridges) is also fouled if submerged, even if the weapon lacks the misfire property.

Some firearms list a number parenthetically after the misfire property. If the d20 for your attack roll is equal to or lower than the number indicated, prior to any modifiers, the weapon's barrel is fouled. When a natural 1 is not rolled, it is possible for such an attack to hit its target and still result in a fouled barrel.
If you have a class feature that increases a weapon's misfire rating, and the firearm lacks this property, add the misfire property with a rating equal to what the increase would have been.

name: Misfire
entries: If you roll equal to or lower than a weapon's misfire rating (noted in parentheses), the weapon jams as its ammunition fails. The attack automatically misses, and the weapon cannot be used again unless you use an action or a bonus action to clear the chamber and fix whatever caused the weapon to misfire.

entries.name: Momentum
entries: Momentum weapons allow you to deliver devastating attacks as part of rapid movement. When you hit with a Momentum weapon after you moved 20 feet or more in a straight line during the same turn, upgrade the damage dice to the weapon's Momentum Dice value.

entries.name: Natatorial
entries: The {@quickref Underwater Combat|PHB|3} rules do not impose disadvantage on attack rolls with this weapon. All other restrictions apply as normal.

name: Power Cost
entries: The weapon requires 1 or more charges from a myrmidon's arcane condenser to fire, noted in parentheses.

entries.name: Powered
entries: You can activate a Powered weapon that has a charged {@item Power Cell|NeonOdyssey} when you make an attack with it. On a hit when activated, the weapon's damage die changes to the value noted with the property. If a damage type is also noted, the weapon deals damage of that type when activated. If the weapon has the {@itemProperty V|XPHB|Versatile} property, the Powered property has a second notation for the activated damage when wielded with two hands.
A fully charged {@item Power Cell|NeonOdyssey} operates the weapon for 25 activated attacks, after which you must replace the cell as an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Psiactive
entries: A psiactive ranged weapon draws its power from your innate psionic potential, whether or not you're trained to use it. When attacking with a psiactive weapon, you use your choice of your Intelligence or Charisma modifier for the attack and damage rolls.

You can fire psiactive weapons a number of times equal to twice your proficiency bonus. After that, your psionic potential is temporarily expended and you can't fire another psiactive weapon until you regain your psionic focus by using an action or a bonus action (your choice). Your psionic focus is shared between all psiactive weapons; whenever you make an attack with any psiactive weapon, you expend one of your uses.

As psiactive weapons channel your own latent energy, they aren't considered magic weapons and they can't be sensed with the {@spell detect magic} spell or similar magic. However, they don't function in an {@spell antimagic field}.

name: Psionic
entries: {@note This item's power is psionic in nature.}

entries.name: Psionic Crystal
entries: Psionic items use the same categories as magic items, but add one additional category—psionic crystal, a consumable psionic item akin to potions or spell scrolls. A creature can use an action to break one of these applesized crystals, unleashing the psionic power stored within.

entries.name: Pugilist
entries: For creatures that roll a die when they make unarmed strikes (such as the {@class monk|PHB} or {@subclass TavernBrawler|Fighter|PHB|LALoTT|tavern brawler fighter}), the size of their damage die is increased by one (maximum 1d12) when they make unarmed strikes with a hand equipped with a weapon that has this property.

name: quick-escape
entries: {@i This suit of armor, or its bulkiest portions, can be removed with a single action. This is advantageous when the armor might inhibit the wearer's swimming, or it has been affected by a heat metal spell.}
Donning the suit is no faster than normal.

entries.name: Recoil
entries: After you make an attack with this weapon, you can't make ranged attacks beyond the weapon's normal range until the end of the current turn.

entries.name: Recoil
entries: After you make an attack with this weapon, you can't make ranged attacks beyond the weapon's normal range until the end of the current turn.

name: reinforced
entries: {@i This armor redoubles its protection over certain vulnerable spots.}
Weapon attacks made against the wearer do not benefit from the {@item deadly weapon|CompEquipMan|deadly} or {@item high-critical weapon|CompEquipMan|high-critical} weapon properties.

entries.name: Reload
entries: Some ranged weapons can be fired a number of times before they must be reloaded. Ranged weapons with the reload property take an action (player's choice) to reload its ammunition.
If you wield two light ranged weapons with the reload property, you can reload them both at once as an action during your turn.

entries.name: Reload
entries: A limited number of shots can be made with a weapon that has the reload property. A character must then reload it using an action or a bonus action (the character's choice).

entries.name: Reload
entries: A Reload weapon's ammunition is held in a magazine or a {@item Power Cell|NeonOdyssey}. After the number of shots noted in the property, you must reload the weapon as an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Reload
entries: This weapon can be used to make a number of attacks before it must be reloaded. If you are proficient with the weapon, reloading it takes an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}; otherwise, reloading it takes an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}.

name: Reload
entries: This weapon can be used to make a number of attacks before it must be reloaded. If you are proficient with the weapon, reloading it takes an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}; otherwise, reloading it takes an action. The number of attacks is determined by the size of the weapon's damage die or dice, as shown on the Reload Attacks table.

entries.name: Reload
entries: A limited number of shots, specified by the number in parentheses after the reload property, can be made with this weapon. A character must then reload it using an action.

entries.name: Reload
entries: A number of pieces of ammunition, specified by the number in parentheses after the Reload property, can be loaded into this weapon. Making a ranged attack with the weapon uses one piece of ammunition from the amount within. When the weapon has no ammunition left, a creature must use an action to reload it before it can be used to make ranged attacks again. A creature can reload a weapon before it runs out of ammunition, replacing or adding to the ammunition already inside, up to the maximum amount the weapon can hold.
A creature can use magical or specialised ammunition that has been loaded into the weapon for any ranged attack made with the weapon (creature's choice for each attack).

entries.name: Reload 5
entries: This weapon must be reloaded as an action or a bonus action after firing 5 times.

entries.name: Repeater
entries: Repeater weapons can fire ammo in quick succession, using multiple barrels or quick-reloading mechanisms. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action with a Repeater weapon, you can shoot multiple times if you have features that let you attack more than once as part of that action, such as Extra Attack. After taking the {@action Attack|XPHB} action you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to attack once with the same weapon. You don't add your ability modifier to the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}'s attack, unless that modifier is negative.

name: Sacral
entries: A weapon with the Sacral property can be used as a spellcasting focus for blood witch spells. These ritual implements are regularly consecrated in the fresh blood of sacrifices.

entries.name: Scatter
entries: Firearms with the scatter property have two types of damage, a regular damage roll and a scatter damage roll. When you hit a creature with a firearm that has the scatter property, creatures within 5 feet of the target take scatter damage if the attack would hit them. The original target does not take this damage.
You gain resistance to the scatter damage dealt from your firearm attacks.
A spell cast using a firearm with the scatter property only triggers once, and only on the original target of the attack.
{@footnote (see the blood-lightning shot spell)|{@note This spell is not provided in the document.}}

entries.name: Scatter
entries: As an action, you can expend 2 shots from the weapon to fire it in a {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} within the specified area. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take damage. Roll the weapon's damage once, and apply it to each creature that failed the save.

entriesTemplate.name: Strength Required
entries: This shield can't be wielded by a creature with a Strength score less than {{item.strength}}.

entries.name: Siege
entries: This weapon deals double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: Recipe
entries: A successful Wisdom ({@skill Cooking|Arcadia11}) check grants a benefit to creatures who eat the prepared food. If the check succeeds by 5 or more, the recipe is delicious, granting an alternate benefit a creature may choose instead. If the {@dice d20} roll for the check is 20 and the check succeeds, the recipe is extra delicious, granting both previous benefits or a third alternative (as noted in the recipe).

entries.name: Reload (Slow)
entries: A limited number of shots can be made with a weapon that has the slow reload property. A character must then reload it using an action.

entries.name: Slow Reload
entries: You must use an attack or an action to reload this firearm. You must have one free hand to do so.

entries.name: Recipe
entries: A successful Wisdom ({@skill Cooking|Arcadia11}) check grants a benefit to creatures who eat the prepared food. If the check succeeds by 5 or more, the recipe is delicious, granting an alternate benefit a creature may choose instead. If the {@dice d20} roll for the check is 20 and the check succeeds, the recipe is extra delicious, granting both previous benefits or a third alternative (as noted in the recipe).

entries.name: Spread Fire
entries: A weapon that has the Spread Fire property can't make a normal attack. It instead sprays a {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} with a length equal to its range (for example, a {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP} with a range of 20 feet will fire in a 20-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}). Each creature in the area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take the weapon's normal damage.

entries.name: Spread Fire
entries: A weapon that has the spread fire property can't make a normal attack, instead spraying a cone in front of you with a length equal to its range (for example, a blunderbuss with 'range 20' will fire in a 20-foot cone in front of you). Each creature in the area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your Firearm save DC or take the weapon's normal damage.

entries.name: Spread Fire
entries: A weapon that has the Spread Fire property can't make a normal attack. It instead sprays a {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} with a length equal to its range (for example, a {@item Blunderbuss|SGttEH24} with a range of 20 feet will fire in a 20-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}). Each creature in the area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take the weapon's normal damage.

entries.name: Steady
entries: A weapon with this property can be stabilized for greater accuracy. As a bonus action, you give yourself a bonus to your next attack roll with this weapon this turn equal to your proficiency bonus, and attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You can use this bonus action only if you haven't moved during your turn, and after you use the bonus action, your speed is halved until the end of your turn.

entries.name: Steady
entries: A weapon with this property can be stabilized for greater accuracy. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you give yourself a bonus to your next attack roll with this weapon this turn equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and attacking at the weapon's long range doesn't impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll. You can take this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} only if you haven't moved during your turn, and after you take the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved until the end of your turn.

name: Stealth
entries: You have disadvantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks when wearing this armour.

name: Storm
entries: As a bonus action, you can activate or deactivate this weapon. While activated, this weapon deals 1d4 lightning damage in addition to its normal damage. Each time you make an attack with this weapon while it is activated, you suffer 1d4 lightning damage after resolving the attack.

entries.name: Stormcharged
entries: When you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to attack with a Stormcharged Weapon, you can make only one Attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make. If you could otherwise make additional attacks with that action, the weapon deals an extra 3d6 lightning or thunder damage per attack that was foregone.

name: subtle
entries: This armor takes on the appearance of normal, bulky clothing. Leather padding can be sewn inside canvas tunics and baggy trousers. Chain can be disguised with quilting. Even narrow plates and splinting can be incorporated into the lining of heavy coats. Alternately, the armor is crafted for easy concealment under normal clothing.

This modification can apply to most armor suits, excluding half plate and plate. Heavy or medium armor with this addition can be identified with a {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check by anyone within 30 feet. Physically handling any kind of subtle armor reveals its nature without a check.

entries.name: Thrown Versatility
entries: This weapon is better used for thrown ranged weapon attacks than for melee weapon attacks. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property— the damage when the weapon is used to make a ranged weapon attack.

entries.name: Tiny
entries: These weapons are designed for Tiny creatures. Wielders of all sizes can use such weapons without penalty.
A Tiny creature cannot normally wield a weapon that lacks this property.

entries.name: Trip
entries: This weapon can be used to trip a creature, knocking it {@condition prone}. It uses the same rules as {@action shove|PHB|Shoving a Creature}. However, you cannot use this weapon to push a creature away.

entries.name: Tripping
entries: While wielding this weapon, you gain a +2 bonus on your Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks for {@action Shove|PHB|shoving} a creature if you are attempting to knock it {@condition prone}. Increase this bonus to +3 if the weapon is two-handed (or is versatile and used in two hands), or if you are wielding two single-handed weapons that each have this property.
These benefits do not apply to a {@optfeature Trip Attack|PHB} Combat Maneuver, which uses unrelated techniques to both trip and inflict damage with the same strike.

entries.name: Twinned Barrel
entries: A Twinned Barrel weapon has two barrels that can each hold a {@item firearm bullet|XPHB} and can both be loaded as part of reloading the weapon. You can fire both barrels of a Twinned Barrel weapon as part of an attack, instead of each barrel individually. Doing so empties both barrels of the weapon (as per the {@itemProperty SGEHPP:Bar|SGEHPP|Barrel} property) and increases the damage die of the weapon on a hit (from {@dice d4} to {@dice d6} to {@dice d8} to {@dice d10} to {@dice d12}).

entries.name: Twinned Barrel
entries: This weapon has two barrels that can each hold a bullet and can both be loaded as part of reloading the weapon. You can fire both barrels of a double barrel weapon as part of an attack, instead of each barrel individually. Doing so empties the barrel of the weapon (as per the Barrel property) but increases the damage die of the weapon on a hit (from {@damage d4} to {@damage d6} to {@damage d8} to {@damage d10} to {@damage d12}).

entries.name: Twinned Barrel
entries: A Twinned Barrel weapon has two barrels that can each hold a {@item Bullet|SGttEH24} and can both be loaded as part of reloading the weapon. You can fire both barrels of a Twinned Barrel weapon as part of an attack, instead of each barrel individually. Doing so empties both barrels of the weapon (as per the {@itemProperty SGttEH:Bar|SGttEH24|Barrel} property) and increases the damage die of the weapon on a hit (from {@dice d4} to {@dice d6} to {@dice d8} to {@dice d10} to {@dice d12}).

entries.name: Unarmed (B)
entries: Devices with the unarmed property are not gripped in the hand so do not prevent the wearer from holding something else or otherwise using the affected hand. A device with this property requires an action to put on or remove, a task that requires both hands. It cannot be disarmed.

entries.name: Unarmed (B)
entries: A device with this property affixes to the knuckles, fingers, or the back of the hand. It often takes the form of a glove. Sometimes it is a set of finger rings (connected or unconnected) that are quite heavy or bear sharp protrusions.

This device can modify the wearer's unarmed attacks. If this weapon property is noted (P) or (S), unarmed strikes using the device may inflict piercing or slashing damage instead of bludgeoning damage. This device doesn't restrict the user's unarmed attacks, which can be made with other body parts.

Devices with the unarmed property are not gripped in the hand so do not prevent the wearer from holding something else or otherwise using the affected hand. A device with this property requires an action to put on or remove, a task that requires both hands. It cannot be disarmed.
Unarmed devices can be made magical as weapons can. They can also be silvered or otherwise constructed of exotic materials, increasing the efficacy and versatility of your unarmed strikes.

entries.name: Unarmed (P)
entries: This device can modify the wearer's unarmed attacks to inflict piercing damage instead of bludgeoning damage. This device doesn't restrict the user's unarmed attacks, which can be made with other body parts.

Devices with the unarmed property are not gripped in the hand so do not prevent the wearer from holding something else or otherwise using the affected hand. A device with this property requires an action to put on or remove, a task that requires both hands. It cannot be disarmed.

entries.name: Unarmed (P)
entries: A device with this property affixes to the knuckles, fingers, or the back of the hand. It often takes the form of a glove. Sometimes it is a set of finger rings (connected or unconnected) that are quite heavy or bear sharp protrusions.

This device can modify the wearer's unarmed attacks. If this weapon property is noted (P) or (S), unarmed strikes using the device may inflict piercing or slashing damage instead of bludgeoning damage. This device doesn't restrict the user's unarmed attacks, which can be made with other body parts.

Devices with the unarmed property are not gripped in the hand so do not prevent the wearer from holding something else or otherwise using the affected hand. A device with this property requires an action to put on or remove, a task that requires both hands. It cannot be disarmed.
Unarmed devices can be made magical as weapons can. They can also be silvered or otherwise constructed of exotic materials, increasing the efficacy and versatility of your unarmed strikes.

entries.name: Unarmed (S)
entries: This device can modify the wearer's unarmed attacks to inflict slashing damage instead of bludgeoning damage. This device doesn't restrict the user's unarmed attacks, which can be made with other body parts.

Devices with the unarmed property are not gripped in the hand so do not prevent the wearer from holding something else or otherwise using the affected hand. A device with this property requires an action to put on or remove, a task that requires both hands. It cannot be disarmed.

entries.name: Unarmed (S)
entries: A device with this property affixes to the knuckles, fingers, or the back of the hand. It often takes the form of a glove. Sometimes it is a set of finger rings (connected or unconnected) that are quite heavy or bear sharp protrusions.

This device can modify the wearer's unarmed attacks. If this weapon property is noted (P) or (S), unarmed strikes using the device may inflict piercing or slashing damage instead of bludgeoning damage. This device doesn't restrict the user's unarmed attacks, which can be made with other body parts.

Devices with the unarmed property are not gripped in the hand so do not prevent the wearer from holding something else or otherwise using the affected hand. A device with this property requires an action to put on or remove, a task that requires both hands. It cannot be disarmed.
Unarmed devices can be made magical as weapons can. They can also be silvered or otherwise constructed of exotic materials, increasing the efficacy and versatility of your unarmed strikes.

entries.name: Unarmed
entries: When you make an unarmed strike, you can choose to deal the damage of this weapon instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

entries.name: Bleeder
entries: When hit by a weapon with the bleeder property the target gains the Bleeding condition and the Target takes an additional point of damage of the weapon's type at the start of its next turn until they make a Constitution Save versus (base DC 12 (+ any magical bonuses)), are magical healed, or have

entries.name: Entnagle
entries: Some weapons, particularly those with lengths of rope or chains, are designed to wrap around a foe's weapon or limbs.

A creature can use an attack with such a weapon to entangle the target's weapon or limbs. The attacker makes an attack roll contested by the target's Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. The target has advantage on its ability check if it is larger than the attacking creature, or disadvantage if it is smaller. If the attacker wins the contest, the attack causes no damage or other ill effect, but becomes entangled by the attacker.

An entangled creature has disadvantage on attack rolls until the attacker ends the entanglement with a bonus action; the attacker drops their weapon or the attacker is {@condition incapacitated}; forced movement causes the attacker and target apart beyond the reach of the weapon; or the target uses its action to escape (as though {@condition grappled}). While entangled, neither the attacker nor the target can move apart beyond the reach of the weapon.
While the attacker is entangling the target's weapon, it has advantage on subsequent attempts to disarm the target (see DMG p. 271)

entries.name: Entagled
entries: Some weapons, particularly those with chains, are designed to wrap around a foe's weapon or limbs.

A creature can use an attack with such a weapon to entangle the target's weapon or limbs. The attacker makes an attack roll contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) check or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. The target has disadvantage on its ability check if it is larger than the attacking creature, or advantage if it is smaller.
If the attacker wins the contest, the target becomes entangled (gains the grappled condition) by the attacker.

An entangled creature has disadvantage on attack rolls until the attacker ends the entanglement with a bonus action; the attacker drops their weapon or is incapacitated; forced movement causes the attacker and target to move beyond the reach of the weapon; or the target uses its action to escape (as though grappled).
While entangled, neither the target can move apart beyond the reach of the weapon. The attacker however can drop and move.
While the attacker is entangling the target's weapon, it has advantage on subsequent attempts to attack or disarm the target (see DMG p. 271)

entries.name: Fragile
entries: When a weapon with the fragile property gets a Natural 1, or becomes disarmed. The weapon gains an negative modifier -1 to damage (if weapon damage becomes 0, it breaks)

entries.name: Oversized
entries: A weapon with the oversized property is larger than even the largest conventional weapon. Only individuals with exceptional strength can hope to wield one efficiently.

An oversized weapon counts also as a heavy weapon (PHB p. 147); with the following changes. Both Small and Medium creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls with oversized weapons. A Medium creature does not have disadvantage if its Strength score is 20 or greater.

If a damage value in parenthesis appears with the oversized property, a Large creature may wield the weapon in one or two hands. The oversized damage value is used if the creature wields the weapon in two hands.

entries.name: Undersized
entries: A weapon with the undersized property is particularly small. They can be easily hidden, and are favoured by tiny races.

An undersized one-handed weapon is considered to be a light weapon (PHB p. 147). A Tiny creature can wield an undersized weapon in their off-hand and use it when two-weapon fighting. The weapon deals 1/2 damage from its full sized archetype.
An undersized two-handed weapon can be used by a Tiny creature without taking Disadvantage on their attack rolls. Or by other (Small; Medium) creatures as as one handed.

entries.name: Loading
entries: As a bonus action you switch the ammo your bowgun is using with another. {@i This replaces the standard 5e loading property}.

entries.name: Jewelry
entries: A piece of Jewelry.
Personal ornaments, such as necklaces, rings, or bracelets, that are typically made from or contain jewels and precious metal.

entries.name: Tattoo
entries: A Magical Tattoo. Look at the Books on 5eTools for variant rules for how to acquire, design and include tattoo magic within your campaign.

entries.name: Recharge (X)
entries: Only X attacks can be made with a weapon that has the recharge property before it needs to be recharged. A weapon can be recharged as a bonus action (even if it still has charges left), but it cannot be recharged on the same turn it is used to make an attack.

entries.name: Special
entries: If you have the {@classFeature Martial Arts|Monk||1} feature, wielding a knuckleduster counts as an unarmed strike rather than a weapon attack. Any special properties of the knuckleduster are applied to your unarmed strike.

entries.name: Loud
entries: This weapon makes a loud noise whenever it is used to attack. This noise can be heard over long distances and can give away the location of its wielder.

entries.name: Scatter
entries: This weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d8} piercing damage on a successful hit if the target is not at long range.

entries.name: Special
entries: On a miss, the boomerang returns to the thrower's hand.

entries.name: Arcanic
entries: Arcanic weapons fire bolts of arcane energy without expending ammunition, instead drawing some mana from the user and expelling it as a powerful arcane blast. You can use a weapon that has the arcanic property to make a ranged attack, using the range in parentheses after the property. Despite their magical nature, arcanic weapons do not bypass resistance or immunity to nonmagical damage, unless they are a magical weapon.

entries.name: Burst
entries: The spread weapon area for a burst weapon is a 10-foot cube originating from a target location within the weapon's normal range.

entries.name: Minimum Charisma Requirement (11)
entries: This weapon requires a Charisma score of 11 or higher to wield effectively. A creature attacking with this weapon that does not meet the requirement makes the attack with disadvantage, and if the weapon has the Spread property, they cannot use its special attack.

entries.name: Cleave
entries: The spread weapon area for a cleave weapon is a 10-foot-radius circle centered on you.

entries.name: Close-quarters
entries: When making a ranged attack with a close-quarters weapon against a target within 5 feet, you don't suffer disadvantage on the attack roll as a result of being in close combat.

entries.name: Defender
entries: Weapons with the defender property also count as shields, though they only grant a +1 bonus to AC. You can benefit from only one weapon with the defender property or one shield at a time. Making an attack with any weapon that lacks the defender property changes your stance, preventing you from gaining the AC bonus of a defender weapon until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Minimum Dexterity Requirement (11)
entries: This weapon requires a Dexterity score of 11 or higher to wield effectively. A creature attacking with this weapon that does not meet the requirement makes the attack with disadvantage, and if the weapon has the Spread property, they cannot use its special attack.

entries.name: Minimum Dexterity Requirement (13)
entries: This weapon requires a Dexterity score of 13 or higher to wield effectively. A creature attacking with this weapon that does not meet the requirement makes the attack with disadvantage, and if the weapon has the Spread property, they cannot use its special attack.

entries.name: Erupt
entries: The spread weapon area for an erupt weapon is a 15-foot cone originating from the weapon in a direction of your choice.

entries.name: Heavy Armor Improvement
entries: Once a character reaches 5th level, the base AC of heavy armor increases by 2, representing your character's increased proficiency in them. The maximum bonus to AC from Strength remains +3.

entries.name: Minimum Intelligence Requirement (11)
entries: This weapon requires an Intelligence score of 11 or higher to wield effectively. A creature attacking with this weapon that does not meet the requirement makes the attack with disadvantage, and if the weapon has the Spread property, they cannot use its special attack.

entries.name: Minimum Intelligence Requirement (13)
entries: This weapon requires a Intelligence score of 13 or higher to wield effectively. A creature attacking with this weapon that does not meet the requirement makes the attack with disadvantage, and if the weapon has the Spread property, they cannot use its special attack.

entries.name: Medium Armor Improvement
entries: Once a character reaches 5th level, the base AC of medium armor increases by 1, representing your character's increased proficiency in them. The maximum bonus to AC from Dexterity remains +2.

entries.name: Pierce
entries: The spread weapon area for a pierce weapon is a 1-foot wide line towards a target location within the weapon's normal range.

entries.name: Siege
entries: This weapon deals double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: Spread
entries: When taking the attack action with a spread weapon, you can make a special attack that hits multiple creatures. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the attack action, this attack replaces one of them. When you make this special attack, you can force all creatures within a specific area to make a Dexterity saving throw:

entries.name: Spread weapon save
entries.text: 8 + your normal attack roll modifier for the weapon

entries: On a failed save, a creature takes the damage listed in the parentheses next to the property, plus your ability modifier. You also add any other static damage bonuses that apply to your weapon's damage roll, such as from rage, a fighting style, or a +1 weapon (but not any extra dice).

When a creature fails their saving throw against one of your spread attacks, it counts as a successful hit for features and items (but not spells) that trigger on a hit weapon attack. When you use such effects, apply them to all targets that failed their saving throw and that would have been eligible if you had hit a normal attack with the weapon against them. If the feature or item adds extra damage in the form of dice—such as {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue||1}, {@classFeature Divine Smite|Paladin||2}, or the {@class fighter||Weaponforger's|Weaponforger|ccg} {@filter Weapon Mods|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=WM}, roll one less damage dice than usual when triggering those features this way (a minimum of one extra die).

entries.name: Minimum Strength Requirement (11)
entries: This weapon requires a Strength score of 11 or higher to wield effectively. A creature attacking with this weapon that does not meet the requirement makes the attack with disadvantage, and if the weapon has the Spread property, they cannot use its special attack.

entries.name: Minimum Strength Requirement (13)
entries: This weapon requires a Strength score of 13 or higher to wield effectively. A creature attacking with this weapon that does not meet the requirement makes the attack with disadvantage, and if the weapon has the Spread property, they cannot use its special attack.

entries.name: Minimum Wisdom Requirement (11)
entries: This weapon requires a Wisdom score of 11 or higher to wield effectively. A creature attacking with this weapon that does not meet the requirement makes the attack with disadvantage, and if the weapon has the Spread property, they cannot use its special attack.

entries.name: Psiactive
entries: A psiactive ranged weapon draws its power from your innate psionic potential, whether or not you're trained to use it. When attacking with a psiactive weapon, you use your choice of your Intelligence or Charisma modifier for the attack and damage rolls.

You can fire psiactive weapons a number of times equal to twice your proficiency bonus. After that, your psionic potential is temporarily expended and you can't fire another psiactive weapon until you regain your psionic focus by using an action or a bonus action (your choice). Your psionic focus is shared between all psiactive weapons; whenever you make an attack with any psiactive weapon, you expend one of your uses.

As psiactive weapons channel your own latent energy, they aren't considered magic weapons and they can't be sensed with the {@spell detect magic} spell or similar magic. However, they don't function in an {@spell antimagic field}.

entries.name: Spiked
entries: When hit by a weapon with the spiked property the target gains {@dice +1} damage.

entries.name: Flicker
entries: No characters are proficient in Flicker weapons by default. Flicker weapons come with a special Aura property which can only be used if you are proficient with the weapon.

entries.name: Automatic
entries: When you make an attack with this weapon on your turn, you can choose to make two attacks with disadvantage instead. These attacks always have disadvantage, regardless of circumstance.

entries.name: Blaster
entries: Blasters are arcane weapons that eschew traditional projectiles in favor of energetic pulses, powered by arcane batteries and focused through specialized apertures. Because they self-recharge, blasters need not ever be reloaded, even though some are prone to overheating.
Unlike other weapons, you don't add your ability modifier to the damage roll of a blaster unless otherwise stated.
Unlike other ranged weapons, you can engage in two- weapon fighting with two light blasters. When you do so, you subtract 2 from the damage roll of the bonus attack, to a minimum of 1 damage.

entries.name: Deployable
entries: A deployable weapon releases a type of ammunition that separates from the ship, which might have a movement speed of its own, noted in parentheses. When you make an attack using one of these weapons, you deploy the weapon within your ship's space. You make an attack roll using this weapon when it contacts another ship.

If you use a deployable weapon that has a movement speed, you can choose the direction it travels as a bonus action on your turn. A deployable weapon has a maneuverability of 90 degrees and begins facing in the same direction as the ship. Once a deployable weapon moves for 3 turns, it deactivates and begins drifting listlessly.
Deployable weapons can be targeted independently during flight. Each of these weapons has Armor Class 10 and 1 mega hit point.

entries.name: Explosive
entries: When this weapon's projectile hits a target, it explodes in a 5-foot radius. The projectile can be fired at an unoccupied space within its range. Each creature other than the target within the blast radius must succeed on a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw, taking half the damage rolled on a failed save or no damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Foregrip
entries: This weapon can be used with one or two hands. If used in two hands, its normal range increases by 50 feet and its long range increases by 200 feet.

entries.name: Fist
entries: Attacks made with this weapon are treated as unarmed strikes.

entries.name: Fixed
entries: This weapon is mounted on one side of a ship and can only make attacks against targets within a 90-degree cone in the direction it is facing.

entries.name: Heat
entries: This weapon gains a heat point whenever an attack is made with it and loses one heat point whenever you begin your turn. If the weapon gains 3 heat points, it overheats and loses all heat points. An overheated weapon can't be used to make an attack again until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Mounted
entries: This weapon is normally used while attached to a tripod, vehicle, or other bracing mount. You can mount or unmount this weapon as an action. While it is mounted, it can't be moved. It can only be used to make an attack while unmounted if held by a Medium or larger creature with a Strength score of at least 15.

entries.name: Nonlethal
entries: When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points using this weapon, you can choose to knock the creature out, rendering it unconscious, rather than deal a killing blow.

entries.name: Overheat
entries: Once you make an attack with this weapon, it can't be used again to make an attack until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Scatter
entries: If you make an attack against a target that is within half this weapon's normal range, you deal the 'alt' damage value instead of the weapon's normal damage dice.

entries.name: Sighted
entries: This weapon has disadvantage on attack rolls made against targets within 20 feet.

entries.name: Ship
entries: A ship weapon is powered by a ship and must be mounted to one to fire. This weapon can't target any creature or object that is Huge or smaller.

entriesTemplate.name: Elemental
entries: The weapon deals {{item.customProperties.elemental}} additional damage on a hit.

entries.name: Large
entries: Medium creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls with large weapons. Small and Tiny creatures can't make attacks with large weapons. A large weapon's size and bulk make it too large for a Medium creature to use effectively.

entries.name: Bursting
entries: This weapon can be fired in rapid succession. Whenever you take the Attack action and make a ranged weapon attack with this weapon, you can choose to instead make two special attacks with it. When you do, you make each attack roll normally, but forego adding your ability score modifier to the damage rolls of each attack on a hit.

entries.name: Shielded
entries: This weapon has a barrier attached to it. While holding it with both hands, you have a +2 bonus to your AC.

entries.name: Special (Arcane Cannon, Arcane Musket, Dartbow, Slugshooter)
entries: These weapons retain properties of the original weapon, other than the changes listed in the {@quickref weapons} table.
The {@item slugshooter|devikyn-tinker} can't load any ammunition except sling bullets.

entries.name: Double
entries: When you take the Attack action and attack with a double weapon that you're holding, you can use a bonus action to attack again with the other part of the weapon. You don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative.

entries.name: Exotic
entries: No characters are proficient with exotic weapons by default. To become proficient with an exotic weapon, a character must be trained in the use of that specific weapon.

entries.name: Improved Critical
entries: When you score a critical hit with a weapon attack using this weapon, roll the weapon dice three times instead of twice.

entries.name: Broken
entries: A broken firearm cannot be fired until it is repaired. To repair a broken firearm, you may use an action to attempt a tinker's tools ability check with a DC equal to 10 plus the weapon's base misfire score. On a success, the weapon is no longer considered broken.

entries.name: Capacity
entries: A firearm's capacity is the number of shots it can hold at one time. When a firearm has been fired a number of times equal to its capacity, it must be reloaded before firing again.

entries.name: Misfire
entries: If your natural roll for a ranged attack falls at or below the misfire score of the firearm you are using, you suffer a misfire. Your attack misses, any ammo you used in the attack is expended, and your firearm becomes broken. You must repair a broken firearm before using it.
If you don't need to make a ranged attack roll when firing a weapon with a misfire score, roll a d20 to determine if it misfires.

entries.name: Magic
entries: Attacks made with this weapon count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

entries.name: Masterwork
entries: You may re-roll damage die of a 1 with this weapon and must use the new roll, even if it is a 1.

entries.name: Overheat
entries: If this weapon misfires it does so violently, injuring whomever is using it. A creature holding this weapon when it misfires takes the weapon's damage for the attack it misfired on.

entries.name: Oversized
entries: This weapon is designed for a large creature, a medium creature has disadvantage on their attack rolls unless they have a Strength score of 15 or greater. Small or smaller creatures are unable to use this weapon.

entries.name: Recharge
entries: After firing this weapon requires time to recharge, this replaces the next attack you would make with the weapon. The weapon is considered recharged at the start of your turn.

entries.name: Reload
entries: Reloading a gun replaces your next attack you would make with the firearm, refilling the ammunition in the gun up to its capacity. If you prefer, you may instead use an action to reload your firearm.

entries.name: Hidden
entries: You have advantage on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks to conceal this weapon.

entries.name: Monk Weapon
entries: A weapon with this property is included in the weapons that you can use with the Monk's Martial Arts feature and Monks are proficient with this weapon in addition to their other weapon proficiencies.
